funFact: Your spine has 33 little bones that stack up like building blocks!
story: A tiny tea party needed a table, so one clever kid turned into the sturdiest table in the land — not even a stack of teacups could wobble it.
description: Hands and knees on the floor — let's build a table! 🛋️ Hands under your shoulders, knees under your hips. Make your back flat as a tabletop. Shhh... steady! Could a teacup balance on your back?

funFact: Real crabs walk sideways because their legs bend that way — try a sideways scuttle!
story: Down on the sunny beach, Coco the Crab lifted her shell high and scuttled sideways to guard her favorite shiny pebble.
description: Sit down, hands behind you, feet flat in front. Now press down and lift your bottom up — snip snip! 🦀 Push your belly toward the sky. Can you take three sideways crab steps?

funFact: Rocking on your back gives your spine a gentle massage, like tiny rolling waves.
story: Grandma Bear's rocking chair creaked back and forth on the porch, rocking faster and faster until it almost rocked right up to standing!
description: Sit down and hug your knees like a cozy package. 🪑 Tuck your chin, round your back like a banana... and rock! Back and forth, wheee! Can you rock all the way back up to sitting?

funFact: The muscles along your spine work like superhero cables holding you tall all day long.
story: High above the city, a young superhero zoomed through the clouds, cape flapping, off to rescue a kitten stuck in a tree.
description: Lie on your tummy, arms stretched out front like you're flying! 🦸 Take a big breath and lift your arms, chest, and legs off the floor. WHOOSH! You're soaring! Hold on, hero... and gently land.

funFact: Lifting your opposite arm and leg makes both sides of your brain work together!
story: Every superhero starts with flying school — first one arm and the opposite leg, then swap sides, until zoom-day arrives.
description: Lie on your tummy like a napping hero. Now lift just your RIGHT arm and LEFT leg — halfway flying! 🦸 Lower down softly... and swap sides. One wing at a time!

funFact: Real rockets have to zoom faster than 40,000 kilometers per hour to leave Earth!
story: Mission control counted down as the little rocket crouched on the launch pad, engines rumbling, ready to blast off to the sparkly moon.
description: Crouch down small, hands pressed together in front like a rocket nose. 🚀 Squeeze your tummy tight — that's your engine! Count down: 3... 2... 1... BLAST OFF! Jump up tall, arms to the stars!

benefits: Helps you feel big and brave
funFact: A starfish can regrow a whole arm if it loses one — how amazing is that?
story: On the ocean floor, Stella the Starfish stretched all five points as wide as she could to catch the warm rays of sunshine wiggling through the water.
description: Lie on your back and spread out W-I-D-E! ⭐ Arms out, legs out — you're a giant starfish! Squeeze every finger and toe out long. Take a big starfish breath... ahhh.

funFact: Castle drawbridges were pulled up with giant chains to keep the castle safe at night.
story: The castle guard shouted 'Ships ahoy!' and the mighty drawbridge slowly lifted to let the boats sail underneath.
description: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat. 🏰 Press your feet down and lift your hips up — the drawbridge is opening! Creeeak! Hold it high... then slowly lower the bridge back down.

funFact: Beetles are the biggest animal family on Earth — there are more kinds of beetles than any other creature!
story: A cheerful little beetle rolled onto its back in the grass and waved its legs at the clouds, giggling as they tickled the breeze.
description: Lie on your back and lift your arms and legs up like a wiggly beetle! 🪲 Keep your back snuggled into the floor. Now slowly reach one arm back and the opposite leg long... and switch! Wiggle wiggle!

funFact: Your biggest breathing muscle, the diaphragm, sits under your lungs like a trampoline.
story: At the birthday party, one magic balloon puffed up big and round, then let its air out slooowly with the tiniest happy whistle.
description: Lie on your back and put your hands on your tummy. 🎈 Breathe in through your nose and puff your belly up like a big balloon! Now breathe out slowly... pfffff... balloon goes flat. Again!

funFact: Practicing a little plank every day makes your muscles remember it — that's called muscle memory!
story: Before the big bear could hold the log bridge steady, the little cub practiced on a shorter bridge — and got stronger every single day.
description: Start on hands and knees, then walk your hands forward a little. 🐻 Keep your knees down and make a straight line from head to knees. Squeeze your tummy — you're a strong baby plank! Hold it, superstar!

funFact: Fancy waiters can carry three plates on one arm without dropping a single pea!
story: In the busiest restaurant in town, the world's steadiest waiter glided between tables balancing a tall wobbly cake — and never dropped a crumb.
description: Start in Table Top, nice and steady. 🍽️ Now lift one arm out in front like you're carrying a pizza tray! Keep your back flat and tummy tight. Hold... and switch arms. Order up!

funFact: The word 'nava' means boat in Sanskrit — sailors in India used boats like this thousands of years ago!
story: A brave little sailboat pushed off from the harbor, tipped back its sail, and balanced perfectly on the sparkly waves all the way to Treasure Island.
description: Sit down, knees bent, and hold on behind your knees. ⛵ Lean back a little and lift your feet up — you're floating! Feeling strong? Stretch your legs and arms out like sails! Rock steady, captain!

funFact: 'Ardha' means half in Sanskrit — lots of poses have a half version to learn first!
story: Before sailing the seven seas, every little boat learns to float in the calm harbor with its sails halfway up.
description: Sit tall, knees bent, feet on the floor. 🛶 Hold behind your knees, lean back a bit, and lift your feet so your shins are flat like a little deck. Tummy strong! You're floating in the harbor!

funFact: 'Phalaka' means plank of wood — your body becomes one strong, straight board!
story: When the river washed the bridge away, one strong kid stretched out like a wooden plank so the ants could march safely across.
description: Start on hands and knees, then step your feet back and straighten your legs. 🌉 Make one straight line from head to heels — strong like a bridge! Squeeze your tummy tight. Don't let the ants fall! Hold... hold... you did it!

funFact: Crocodiles can float perfectly still in the water for hours — that's champion stillness!
story: A sneaky crocodile lay low and flat in the river, still as a log, waiting for the perfect moment to splash its friends.
description: Come down onto your forearms, elbows under your shoulders. 🐊 Step your feet back and make your body one long, low line — you're a floating crocodile! Belly tight, breathe slow... still as a log!

funFact: You have tummy muscles on your sides called obliques — they help you twist and bend!
story: The little sailboat practiced leaning into the wind with one anchor down, getting ready for the day it would sail free.
description: Start on hands and knees. Keep one knee down and stretch the other leg out to the side. 📐 Now reach your top arm to the sky and open up sideways! Strong and steady... then switch sides!

funFact: Every tiger has its own stripe pattern, just like your fingerprint belongs only to you!
story: Deep in the jungle, a young tiger stretched one strong back leg high into the leaves, showing the whole jungle its beautiful stripes.
description: Start in Table Top, paws strong. 🐯 Now sweep one leg up and back behind you, toes to the sky! Lift your chin like a proud tiger. Grrr! Hold it... then switch legs, jungle cat!

funFact: Rounding your back like this gives your spine a lovely stretch in the opposite direction of sitting.
story: A curious snail curled up tight inside its shell to say hello to its own nose, then stretched out long to keep exploring the garden.
description: Start in Table Top. Breathe out and pull one knee toward your nose while you round your back like a shell! 🐌 Squeeze your tummy — can your knee and nose almost touch? Stretch the leg back out... and again!

funFact: Dogs stretch just like this every time they wake up from a nap — it's called a play bow!
story: A happy puppy dreamed it was chasing a bouncy red ball, and its legs started running even in Downward Dog!
description: Start in Downward Dog, bottom high like a mountain. 🐕 Lift one leg up, then swoosh your knee forward toward your nose! Send it back up... and again! You're a dog running in a dream! Switch legs!

funFact: Pointer dogs really do stand like this — one paw up, nose forward — when they spot a bird!
story: In the tall golden grass, a clever dog froze like a statue, one paw lifted, pointing the way to a bright blue bird.
description: Start in Table Top. Now stretch your RIGHT arm forward and your LEFT leg back — point like a bird dog! 🐦 Flat back, tight tummy, steady... steady... Now swap sides. Woof! Tweet!

benefits: Wakes up the back of your body
funFact: This pose is the upside-down twin of Table Top — your belly becomes the tabletop!
story: The playground tables flipped over at midnight and discovered they made excellent slides for the toys.
description: Sit with knees bent, feet flat, hands behind you with fingers pointing toward your feet. 🛝 Press down and lift your hips until your tummy is flat like a table! Let your heart shine up. Strong table!

funFact: Starfish don't have a brain, but they can still move all five arms — your brain controls all four of yours!
story: When the tide tickled her tummy, Stella the Starfish folded two of her points together to catch a passing bubble, then stretched wide again.
description: Lie back in your big starfish X. 🌟 Now crunch! Reach your right hand across to touch your left foot up high. Stretch back out wide... and switch sides! Fold and sparkle, fold and sparkle!

funFact: Gymnasts practice this exact banana shape to get strong enough for flips!
story: One silly banana rolled out of the fruit bowl and rocked happily on the kitchen floor, giggling with every wobble.
description: Lie on your back and lift your arms and legs a little bit off the floor — you're a banana! 🍌 Squeeze your tummy so your back stays cozy on the ground. Now rock gently, tip to tip! Silly banana!

funFact: Swimmers flutter-kick just like this — tiny fast kicks move them through the water!
story: The superhero dove into the sparkling sea to rescue a drifting beach ball, flutter-kicking like a speedboat.
description: Lie on your tummy and lift your arms and legs like a flying hero. 🏊 Now flutter! Little kicks with your legs, little paddles with your arms — swim, hero, swim! Keep breathing... and rest.

funFact: When you lift one hand in plank, your tummy muscles work double to keep you from tipping!
story: Two strong bridges stood side by side over the river and gave each other a high-five every time a boat sailed under.
description: Get into your strong plank. 🖐️ Keep your hips super still... now lift one hand and tap your other shoulder — high-five yourself! Put it back, switch hands. Tap, tap, steady as a statue!

benefits: Stretches the back of your legs
funFact: This move is called an inchworm too — inchworms really do walk by scrunching and stretching!
story: The gardener's wheelbarrow rolled itself out to the vegetable patch every morning, front wheel first, wheels squeaking a happy song.
description: Stand tall, then fold down and put your hands on the floor. 🛞 Walk your hands forward, step by step, until you're in a long plank — you're the wheelbarrow! Now walk your hands back and stand up. Again!

funFact: Bears look slow, but they can sprint faster than the fastest human!
story: A quiet bear cub hovered low over the berry bushes, knees floating, trying not to squash a single berry.
description: Start in Table Top, toes tucked under. 🐻 Now press into your paws and float your knees just a tiny bit off the floor — hover like a sneaky bear! Tummy tight, breathe... hold that hover!

funFact: The lower a boat floats, the more its 'engine' — your tummy — has to work!
story: The speedboat skimmed low over the waves, almost touching the water, engine humming with all its might.
description: Lie back, then lift your shoulders AND legs just a little off the floor — low and long like a speedboat! 🚤 Reach your arms toward your toes. Engine on, tummy strong! Hold... vrrrmmm... and rest.
safetyNote: Keep your lower back pressed toward the floor. Rest the moment your back wants to arch.

funFact: Sailors get 'sea legs' — their bodies learn to balance on rocking waves, just like yours is learning now!
story: A storm of giggles rolled across the sea, and the brave little boat rocked low into the waves and back up tall, never ever tipping over.
description: Float in Boat Pose, arms out like sails. 🌊 Now lower your body and legs toward the floor — big wave! — and lift back up to boat! Down like a wave, up like a sail. Can you ride three waves?
safetyNote: Move slowly with your breath. If your back arches off the boat, make the rocking smaller.

funFact: This pose is named after Vasistha, a wise teacher from ancient Indian stories.
story: A daring surfer tipped their board sideways on the biggest wave of the day and rode it all the way to shore with one arm reaching for the sun.
description: Start in plank, strong and straight. 🏄 Roll onto one hand and the side of your feet, stacking your body sideways. Reach your top arm to the sky! You're surfing! Hold steady... then switch sides.
safetyNote: Keep your bottom hand right under your shoulder. Drop your bottom knee down any time you need.

funFact: Your side tummy muscles help you every time you carry a heavy backpack on one shoulder.
story: The skier leaned into the mountainside, one arm braced on the snow, holding strong while the wind whooshed past.
description: Lie on your side, propped up on your forearm, elbow under your shoulder. ⛷️ Stack your feet and lift your hips high — one strong sideways line! Top arm up! Hold... whoosh... then switch sides.
safetyNote: Keep your elbow under your shoulder. Lower your hips and rest if your shoulder gets tired.

benefits: Strengthens the back of your body
funFact: 'Purva' means east — this pose stretches the front of your body toward the rising sun!
story: As the sun rose over the sea, one strong kid turned into an upside-down bridge so the morning light could sparkle across their whole front.
description: Sit with legs long, hands behind you, fingers pointing to your toes. 🌅 Press down and lift your hips waaay up — your whole body is one straight sunny ramp! Point your toes and shine! Hold... and lower gently.
safetyNote: Keep your chin gently tucked instead of dropping your head all the way back. Skip if wrists hurt.

funFact: Balancing on one arm makes your tummy muscles work twice as hard to keep you level!
story: The bridge keeper held the whole bridge steady with one mighty arm while waving hello to the boats with the other.
description: Make your strongest plank, feet a little wider. 💪 Squeeze your tummy tight... now stretch one arm straight out in front like a superhero! Keep your hips level — no tipping! Hold... and switch arms.
safetyNote: Widen your feet for balance and keep hips level. Rest your knees down if you start to sag.

funFact: 'Eka pada' means one foot in Sanskrit — lots of one-legged poses share this name!
story: The strong plank bridge lifted one end to let a family of ducks waddle underneath, and never wobbled once.
description: Start in your best plank. 🦵 Squeeze everything strong... now float one leg up off the floor! Keep your body in one straight line, hips steady. Hold... breathe... switch legs, champion!
safetyNote: Lift the leg only a little — keeping a straight back matters more than lifting high.

funFact: 'Lola' means swinging like a pendulum — the swinging part of a grandfather clock!
story: Inside the great clock tower, the golden pendulum swung tick... tock... lifting itself with magic clockwork muscles.
description: Sit on your heels, hands flat on the floor beside your hips. 🕰️ Press down hard, squeeze your tummy, and try to lift your knees and feet off the ground — even a tiny hop counts! Tick-tock! Can you swing?
safetyNote: Use yoga blocks under your hands to make lifting easier. Tiny lifts are a big win — no swinging high.

funFact: Opening your arms and legs wide in balance poses actually helps some people steady themselves, like a tightrope walker's pole!
story: As night fell, the surfer's board turned into a shooting star, and they stretched out a leg and an arm to sparkle across the sky.
description: Come into your strong Side Plank. ✨ Now lift your top leg up high and reach your top arm to the sky — you're a shining star! Press the floor away, hold that sparkle... and gently come down. Switch sides!
safetyNote: Master regular Side Plank first. Keep the bottom hand under your shoulder and come down slowly.

funFact: 'Tola' means a weighing scale — your whole body balances between your two hands like treasure being weighed!
story: In the marketplace of a golden city, a magical scale lifted itself into the air to weigh a single feather against a wish.
description: Sit with crossed legs, hands flat beside your hips. ⚖️ Take a big breath, press the floor away, squeeze your tummy... and lift your whole seat off the ground! Floating! Hold... and land softly like a feather.
safetyNote: Only with a grown-up nearby. Use blocks under your hands, keep a simple cross-legged seat, and skip full lotus.

funFact: Gymnasts hold L-sits on rings and bars — it's one of the toughest shapes in gymnastics!
story: The letter L jumped right off the alphabet poster and balanced proudly on its own two hands to show everyone how strong letters can be.
description: Sit with your legs straight out, hands flat beside your hips. 🔤 Press down with all your might, tummy super tight... and lift your seat AND legs off the floor — you're a flying letter L! Even one second counts!
safetyNote: Only with a grown-up spotter. Practice on yoga blocks first, and lift just your seat before trying to lift your legs.

funFact: Lifting an opposite arm and leg in plank leaves only two corners holding you up — that's why your tummy has to be the boss!
story: On the tallest rooftop, the greatest superhero balanced on one hand and one foot, cape rippling, watching over the sleeping city.
description: Make your strongest plank, feet wide. 🦅 Squeeze everything... now lift your RIGHT arm forward and your LEFT leg up at the same time! Two corners flying, two corners strong! Hold... land... switch sides, hero!
safetyNote: Only with a grown-up spotter after One-Arm and One-Leg Plank feel easy. Keep lifts small and come down the moment you wobble.
